program.name: Heterogeneous Learning Systems
program.definition: Study of distribution, organization, use, combination and development of heterogeneous capabilities under constraints.

entities.name: Finite static two-task allocation
entities.definition: Two task types with fixed per-agent effectiveness; demand probability p weights task 1.
entities.scope: Exact, finite, two agents and two task types; scalar effectiveness.
assumptions: No learning or time evolution.

scenario_contract.tasks: Two task types with demand probability p for task 1
scenario_contract.constraints: Compare a common agent across tasks against taskwise access
scenario_contract.uncertainty: No stochastic outcome mechanism required; expected effectiveness is evaluated.

entities.name: Finite effectiveness–resource allocation
entities.definition: Two tasks and agent-specific effectiveness/resource pairs under a fixed resource budget.
entities.scope: Exact finite convexified time-sharing controls.
assumptions: Linear mixing is admissible for the convexified cases.

scenario_contract.capabilities: Fixed effectiveness and resource pair per agent-task
scenario_contract.constraints: Resource budget; time-sharing only where explicitly admissible

entities.name: Two-period competence development
entities.definition: Two agents, two task types and two decision periods; action-dependent change in one competence coordinate.
entities.scope: Deterministic finite analytical testbed.
assumptions: Learning-by-doing transition and terminal routing exactly as specified in THEORY.md.

scenario_contract.tasks: Two task types over two decision periods
scenario_contract.uncertainty: None in the retained exact construction.

entities.name: Synthetic deadline-constrained task queues
entities.definition: Poisson task arrivals, four task families, FCFS single-agent queues, lognormal service and a three-unit deadline.
entities.scope: Synthetic event-driven scenario; three scales and phase-varying demand in the confirmatory study.
assumptions: No learning/cooperation; all conclusions are model-scoped.

scenario_contract.tasks: Four task families arriving in continuous time
scenario_contract.capabilities: Correctness probabilities by agent and task family
scenario_contract.dynamics: Poisson arrivals; service completion and queues
scenario_contract.constraints: FCFS, one service per agent, deadline arrival+3, common admission rule
scenario_contract.uncertainty: Poisson arrivals and lognormal service/correctness outcomes.

entities.name: Stationary task-family queue with fixed competence matrix
entities.definition: Twelve agents and four equiprobable task families under a stationary arrival-mark distribution.
entities.scope: Synthetic paired simulation with N=12, fixed P1 and 30 paired seeds.
assumptions: Two specified competence structures only; service/deadline law inherited from the queue model.

scenario_contract.capabilities: Two fixed 12x4 competence matrices with equal per-family means and maxima
scenario_contract.constraints: P1 assignment, FCFS and deadline law inherited from queue scenario

entities.name: Finite sequential problem-belief histories
entities.definition: Sequential FAST/DEEP computations and terminal decision over frozen finite problem-belief domains.
entities.scope: Synthetic confirmatory evaluation across frozen domains/histories.
assumptions: Physical task and observation innovations paired; policy states evolve separately.

scenario_contract.tasks: Finite physical decision problems with sequential computations
scenario_contract.dynamics: Belief/history and computation state evolve by observations
scenario_contract.uncertainty: Frozen finite problem-belief domains and observation innovations.

entities.name: Finite prospective adaptation histories
entities.definition: Finite histories with belief and capability state, policy-dependent decisions and counterfactual continuations.
entities.scope: Synthetic model and frozen reference-state population.
assumptions: Reference-state population is not the full state space.

scenario_contract.tasks: Finite tasks/worlds in a reference-state population
scenario_contract.uncertainty: Finite synthetic worlds; reference population is not full state space.

entities.name: Single-agent task responsibility
entities.definition: One selected agent handles both task types.
entities.scope: Static assignment baseline.
assumptions: Agent identity fixed across task types.

entities.name: Task-wise agent access
entities.definition: A task may be assigned independently to an admissible agent for each type.
entities.scope: Static task routing class.
assumptions: The allowed routing set and any time sharing must be declared.

entities.name: Fixed agent-by-task competence structure
entities.definition: Rows identify agents and columns task families; individual entries remain fixed during evaluation.
entities.scope: General structural representation used by finite and queue models.
assumptions: Entry semantics are model-specific; may be probability or deterministic score.

entities.name: Independent FCFS agent queues
entities.definition: Each agent has one FCFS queue and at most one active task.
entities.scope: Synthetic deadline queue studies.
assumptions: No task cooperation or interruption.

entities.name: Paired generalist and specialist competence matrices
entities.definition: Structure A has three all-high/nine all-low profiles; structure B has three specialists per task family; per-family means/maxima match.
entities.scope: N=12, K=4, values h=.9/l=.6.
assumptions: No claim beyond these two matrices.

entities.name: Static task allocation under heterogeneous effectiveness
entities.definition: Finite model comparing same-agent assignment and task-wise routing for fixed effectiveness.
entities.scope: Two agents/two tasks exact model.
assumptions: Scalar additive expectation over the task mixture.
entities.mathematical_object: 2x2 fixed effectiveness matrix and task-1 demand probability in [0,1]
entities.inputs: Four assignment expected-effectiveness values, same-agent/taskwise maxima, and their difference

entities.name: Effectiveness–resource frontier allocation
entities.definition: Finite set of assignment points, with a resource budget and upper efficient convex hull.
entities.scope: Two agents/two tasks.
assumptions: Convex hull interpretation requires admissible time-sharing and linear outcome/resource mixtures.
entities.mathematical_object: 2x2 effectiveness/resource pairs, task demand probability, resource budget
entities.inputs: Feasible policy points, efficient hulls, and best effectiveness under budget
entities.outputs: Finite bicriterion allocation with optional convexified time-sharing.

entities.name: Two-period endogenous competence development
entities.definition: Action-dependent state transition followed by terminal task routing and demand-weighted future value.
entities.scope: Two agents, two tasks, two periods.
assumptions: Deterministic bounded learning-by-doing; no noise, forgetting, or transfer.
entities.mathematical_object: 2x2 initial competence matrix, action-dependent increments, selected agent, future task mixture
entities.inputs: Post-action competence, terminal assignment outcomes/frontier, immediate/future/total value differences
entities.outputs: Deterministic two-period finite transition and terminal allocation.

entities.name: Dynamic deadline-constrained allocation
entities.definition: Queue state, service times, task correctness, deadline and assignment policy determine on-time collective success.
entities.scope: Synthetic simulator used for confirmatory queue studies.
assumptions: The implementation/results are historical on this branch and not replayable from retained code.
entities.mathematical_object: Task arrivals, queue state, competence matrix or estimates, service-time law, deadlines and policy state
entities.inputs: Agent choice/admission, task completion correctness/timing, collective on-time success and costs
entities.outputs: Discrete-event queue model with one FCFS queue per agent.

entities.name: Sequential computation allocation under belief state
entities.definition: Policy chooses whether to spend additional computation before a terminal decision.
entities.scope: Frozen finite sequential problem-belief design.
assumptions: Different policies induce different histories; randomized baseline did not exactly match realized call counts.
entities.mathematical_object: Finite problem belief/history, computation options, signals, compute cost and stopping choices
entities.inputs: Computation selection, terminal answer, physical reward and compute use
entities.outputs: Sequential decision model; not worker competence allocation.

entities.name: Prospective information and development decision model
entities.definition: Finite belief/capability histories compare myopic and prospective choices with counterfactual continuation.
entities.scope: Frozen synthetic state/reference population.
assumptions: Counterfactual value is model-derived, not an external causal variable.
entities.mathematical_object: Finite state/belief, available information, action-dependent state changes and continuation conditions
entities.inputs: Action choice, counterfactual branch outcomes and model-specific current/future value
entities.outputs: Finite policy and counterfactual models; study-specific state populations.

entities.name: Exact finite model evaluation
entities.definition: Enumerate feasible actions/outcomes and compare exact values/frontiers.
entities.scope: Finite deterministic models.
assumptions: No sampling uncertainty unless stochasticity is explicitly integrated.

entities.name: Paired-replica evaluation
entities.definition: Differences are computed at the independent seed/replica level; bootstrap resamples whole paired replicas.
entities.scope: Simulation campaigns with coupled exogenous/potential outcomes.
assumptions: Tasks inside a replica are not independent replications.

entities.name: Correct completion within deadline rate
entities.definition: Number of tasks both correct and completed by their deadline divided by all arrivals.
entities.scope: Queue/deadline studies.
assumptions: Rejected, wrong, and late tasks count as failures.

entities.name: Static allocation under task-dependent competence
entities.definition: When does task-specific access to fixed competence improve attainable performance?
entities.scope: Finite exact static setting.
assumptions: No learning or dynamics.

entities.name: Crossed specialization exact control
entities.definition: Symmetric two-agent/two-task crossed effectiveness at equal demand.
entities.scope: p=.5; effectiveness entries 1.0 and .2.

entities.name: Exact gain from task-wise allocation in crossed specialization
entities.definition: Task-wise routing obtains effectiveness 1.0 versus .6 for the best one-agent policy; difference .4.
entities.scope: Exact two-agent/two-task instance at p=.5.
assumptions: Fixed effectiveness; scalar additive expected effectiveness.

entities.name: Dynamic competence change and future value
entities.definition: Can action-induced competence change affect the collective frontier, future value, and current choice?
entities.scope: Exact deterministic two-period testbed.
assumptions: No empirical calibration.

entities.name: Learning-induced state change with unchanged efficient frontier
entities.definition: Compare two action-induced terminal states under identical future demand.
entities.scope: Initial state ((.4,.8),(.8,.4)); learning rate (.1,0).

entities.name: Future-value reversal control
entities.definition: Compare current and future value differences in a finite two-period decision.
entities.scope: Initial state ((.7,.8),(.8,.6)); learning rate (.3,0); future task-1 probability .75.

entities.name: State change need not alter efficient collective capability
entities.definition: The two resulting states differ but both frontiers equal {(0.8,0.8)} and future-value difference is zero.
entities.scope: Exact finite construction.

entities.name: Future development value can reverse an immediate preference
entities.definition: At p=.75, immediate difference is -.1, future development value is +.15, and total difference is +.05.
entities.scope: Exact finite construction.

entities.name: Joint and separated policy-class boundary
entities.definition: Under what exact finite assumptions does joint operation/development outperform a restricted separated class?
entities.scope: Common-world finite policy comparison.
assumptions: Common information, actions, rewards, resources and physics; finite attained optima for iff result.

entities.name: Separated policy-class inclusion
entities.definition: A separated class constrained to greedy routing is a subset of the unrestricted joint class; maximizing over a superset cannot lower value.
entities.scope: Common-world/common-information contract.
assumptions: Same feasible world and objective.

entities.name: Sequential computation selection under performance-cost trade-offs
entities.definition: Does prospective computation selection improve cumulative task reward and computation cost in a frozen finite design?
entities.scope: Frozen synthetic problem-belief histories/domains.
assumptions: No exactly matched realized invocation rate; timings machine-sensitive.

entities.name: Scoped sequential computation trade-off
entities.definition: A prospective computation selector versus a nominally equal-rate randomized rule: +.1167 cumulative physical reward/history [0.0310,0.2013] and −.1924 seconds/history [−.3539,−.0228].
entities.scope: Confirmatory paired histories in the frozen design.
assumptions: Intervals are paired history-level intervals as reported.

entities.name: Joint error dependence and collective majority risk
entities.definition: Can joint error dependence change majority risk when individual error marginals are fixed?
entities.scope: Exact three-classifier probability laws.
assumptions: No classifier model inference.

entities.name: Same error marginal, different majority risk
entities.definition: Both joint laws give individual error .20; majority risk is .30 under law A and .20 under law B.
entities.scope: Exact synthetic joint distributions.

entities.name: Transfer and fixed-organization collective performance
entities.definition: Does transfer improve an individual while reducing collective performance, and does reorganization recover it?
entities.scope: Three synthetic binary tasks; 20 paired seeds in second iteration.
assumptions: V1 had target-label leakage; V2 intervals include zero.

entities.name: Transfer advantage and collective effect not established
entities.scope: Twenty paired synthetic seeds.

entities.name: Competence structure, assignment policy and scale in deadline queues
entities.definition: How do mean-preserving competence profiles, allocation policy and scale relate to on-time collective task success?
entities.scope: Synthetic dynamic queue, N=12/24/48, four task families, 30 paired seeds.
assumptions: One synthetic queue/service/deadline model; no learning/cooperation; P1 not globally optimal.

entities.name: Factorial deadline-queue comparison
entities.definition: Three competence compositions × four policies × three scales, 30 seeds; 1080 valid replicas.
entities.scope: Poisson arrivals; lognormal service; FCFS; deadline +3.

entities.name: Mean-preserving profile contrast under information-complete assignment
entities.scope: Thirty paired seeds per scale; synthetic model.

entities.name: Estimated competence lagged the information-complete reference
entities.scope: Thirty paired seeds per scale; synthetic model.

entities.name: External competence calibration and load filtering
entities.definition: How do external calibration and an admissibility load filter affect P2?
entities.scope: Synthetic queue, H2, N=12 and N=48.
assumptions: Results only for one model and selected scales.

entities.name: External calibration improved on-time success in the tested P2 setting
entities.scope: Paired synthetic replicas.

entities.name: Descriptive diagnostics of composition effects
entities.definition: Reanalysis of selection, load and waiting metrics for the deadline-queue factorial.
entities.scope: Reuses 90 existing N=24/P1 replicas.
assumptions: Not an independent replication and no causal mediation identification.

entities.name: Joint competence structure under matched marginals
entities.definition: Do two distinct joint competence matrices with the same per-task mean and maximum differ under fixed allocation?
entities.scope: Stationary synthetic queue; N=12, K=4; 30 paired seeds.
assumptions: Two matrices only; one policy/demand law; no causal mediator established.

entities.name: Paired comparison of two matched-marginal competence structures
entities.definition: Two structures evaluated under the same seed-specific demand and potential outcomes; 60 valid simulation runs.
entities.scope: 30 seed pairs; one N and fixed policy.

entities.name: Different joint structures yielded different performance at equal marginals
entities.definition: B−A success-on-time +21.52 pp, SD 1.13, paired bootstrap 95% interval [21.12,21.92], positive in 30/30 pairs.
entities.scope: Synthetic N=12 queue; 30 paired seeds.
assumptions: Structures have per-family mean .675 and max .9.

entities.name: Assignment sensitivity and future opportunity
entities.definition: Finite analyses of assignment, learning opportunity, and continuation value.
entities.scope: Constructed finite decision processes.
assumptions: No empirical or general-planner validation.

entities.name: Prospective information and development anticipation
entities.definition: Finite adaptation studies compare prospective information/development decisions and realized return.
entities.scope: Frozen synthetic policy and state populations.
assumptions: Conditional reference state bank; exact experiment-specific semantics.

entities.name: Static feasible outcome set
entities.definition: For fixed state, demand, constraints, and admissible policy class, the feasible outcome set is the outcomes induced by feasible policies.
entities.scope: Definition; static model scope.
assumptions: Outcome map and feasibility set must be specified.

entities.name: Crossed-specialization gain formula
entities.definition: Under strict crossed advantage, routing gain is min(p A1,(1-p) A2), with maximum A1 A2/(A1+A2).
entities.scope: Two agents, two tasks, scalar additive effectiveness.
assumptions: Fixed competence and equal-resource model; p is task-1 probability.

entities.name: Competence-state change need not change efficient frontier
entities.definition: Different action-induced states may have identical efficient collective outcome frontiers.
entities.scope: Exact finite counterexample.
assumptions: The frontier is computed from the same terminal routing set.

entities.name: Future capability value depends on future conditions
entities.definition: Different future capabilities can have equal value; a future value difference can reverse an immediate ranking.
entities.scope: Two-period finite construction.
assumptions: Future demand and objective are declared; values are model-specific.

entities.name: Current and continuation value decomposition
entities.definition: In the stated two-period decision, total difference equals current difference plus future development-value difference.
entities.scope: Two-period finite construction and standard continuation value.
assumptions: Common objective and exact transition/value calculation.

entities.name: Joint policy-class value inclusion
entities.definition: Under a common world/information contract, a separated policy class constrained to a subset of actions is contained in the joint class; its maximum value cannot be larger.
entities.scope: Finite common-world decision model.
assumptions: Same feasible world, observations, rewards, resources, objective.

entities.name: Joint error law affects majority risk at fixed individual marginals
entities.definition: Two specified joint laws with marginal error .20 yield majority risks .30 and .20.
entities.scope: Exact three-classifier probability construction.
assumptions: These are the supplied joint laws; not a general theorem about time or AI aging.

entities.name: Finite opportunity-sensitive decisions
entities.definition: Finite state and action constructions in which present assignment can change future opportunity/value.
entities.scope: Synthetic finite decision process.
assumptions: Model-specific transition, information, and continuation-value assumptions.

scenario_contract.dynamics: Finite state transitions and continuation values
scenario_contract.constraints: Model-specific action, information and resource feasibility

entities.name: Assignment sensitivity and continuation value
entities.definition: A finite Bellman analysis connecting an assignment choice to opportunity-dependent continuation value.
entities.scope: Constructed finite states and actions.
assumptions: Local ranking inversion alone does not establish a root-level value gap.
entities.mathematical_object: Finite assignment state/action alternatives, transition and continuation values
entities.inputs: Local ranking and root-level policy value comparisons
entities.outputs: Finite Bellman analysis; local inversion alone is insufficient.

entities.name: Persistence interaction boundary analysis
entities.definition: A planned factorial asked whether architecture, demand persistence and learning interact; a separate fixed-competence fixture evaluated a restricted estimand.
entities.scope: The planned campaign was not run; the retained analytical fixtures are narrower.
assumptions: The fixed-competence fixture does not estimate the unexecuted learning interaction.

entities.name: Competence-improvement priority statistic checks
entities.definition: Exact checks examine whether failure frequency multiplied by quality gap is sufficient to rank improvement opportunities.
entities.scope: Model-specific thresholds, null cases and ranking reversals.
assumptions: No universal priority rule is established.

entities.name: Bounded reproductions of published organization mechanisms
entities.definition: Selected published mechanisms were represented in bounded executable checks to assess correspondence and reuse.
entities.scope: Mechanism-specific bounded reproductions; distinct source mechanisms remain separate.
assumptions: Passing a bounded check is not evidence of general HLS performance.

entities.name: Portfolio learning and interference pilots
entities.definition: Pilot studies examined portfolio learning, opportunity, interference and compatibility in distinct bounded settings.
entities.scope: Multiple protocols and task/data settings; pooled results are not a common estimand.
assumptions: Some cross-protocol comparisons failed compatibility; no general training policy is established.

entities.name: Contextual model selection under quality and latency
entities.definition: A small held-out comparison evaluated dynamic selection among fixed model candidates under quality and latency measurements.
entities.scope: 160 held-out queries; corrected timing and provenance issues are documented.
assumptions: A retrospective oracle is not deployable; small sample and timing limits apply.

entities.name: Model routing under an inference budget
entities.definition: A predictor and a budgeted optimizer were evaluated separately against declared baselines.
entities.scope: Specific predictor/optimizer pilot cells.
assumptions: Predictor and optimizer effects are distinct; one cell does not establish general superiority.

entities.name: Classifier fusion under joint error dependence
entities.definition: Synthetic exact calculations examined coalition accuracy under specified dependence mixtures.
entities.scope: Constructed joint error laws and three-classifier majority examples.
assumptions: No real model inference or general fusion result.

entities.name: Model-specific execution and evaluation contracts
entities.definition: Engineering checks tested bounded provenance-carrying execution/evaluation interfaces across selected model implementations.
entities.scope: Technical vertical slices and contract tests only.
assumptions: Common serialization does not imply mathematical equivalence.

entities.name: Production, competence learning and teaching integration
entities.definition: Bounded model integrations examined production and learning/teaching components with distinct competence and productivity semantics.
entities.scope: Tracked records are incomplete; a larger local artifact was not published and a later campaign was interrupted.
assumptions: Nembhard productivity is not interchangeable with competence; broad outcome is not verifiable.

entities.name: Empirical data vehicle feasibility screening
entities.definition: Feasibility gates assessed whether candidate datasets could support required structural and competence measurements.
entities.scope: Screening only; no empirical validation.
assumptions: No real-world performance claim.

entities.name: State and trajectory discrimination checks
entities.definition: Exploratory gates evaluated whether generated state/trajectory populations had support and discrimination for later comparisons.
entities.scope: Technical diagnostics; not confirmatory policy evaluation.
assumptions: No policy value estimand established.

entities.name: Counterfactual label and engine equivalence gate
entities.definition: A technical gate tested whether counterfactual labels and engine outputs supported a proposed larger comparison; the gate failed.
entities.scope: The planned larger campaign did not execute.
assumptions: A negative gate is not a scientific policy-effect result.

entities.name: Restricted persistence-interaction fixtures
entities.definition: The registered 960-run question was not executed; the fixed-competence stationary equal-marginal fixture has zero expected persistence interaction, while a separate finite fixture reports Θ(1)=−.003.
entities.scope: Analytical fixtures only.

entities.name: Priority statistic lacks universal sufficiency
entities.definition: Exact checks include nulls, thresholds and ranking reversals; they do not validate failure-frequency times quality-gap as a universal selector.
entities.scope: Model-specific exact checks.

entities.name: Bounded mechanism correspondence checks
entities.definition: Selected published mechanisms received bounded executable checks; these do not establish end-to-end HLS performance or general reproduction fidelity.
entities.scope: Technical validation only.

entities.name: Portfolio compatibility and interference findings
entities.definition: Cross-model bridges include failed compatibility, inconclusive portfolio cases and bounded interference/replay findings; protocols do not share one estimand.
entities.scope: Multiple bounded pilots, reported separately in source records.

entities.name: Small held-out model-selection comparison
entities.definition: Corrected comparison reports quality 46.25 versus 45.0 and latency 139.27 versus 141.61 ms; quality difference +1.25 with interval [−1.25,3.75].
entities.scope: 160 held-out queries; timing/provenance corrections apply.

entities.name: Budgeted routing predictor and optimizer results
entities.definition: One predictor scored Brier .2698 versus constant .2314 and logistic .2174; a clear optimizer gain of +2.16 pp was reported in one cell.
entities.scope: Specific pilot configurations only.

entities.name: Synthetic classifier-fusion dependence calculations
entities.definition: Exact mixture check reports coalition accuracy .826 at correlation parameter 0, .700 at 1 and .7945 at .25; separate majority-law result is registered independently.
entities.scope: Constructed synthetic laws; not real inference.

entities.name: Bounded execution-contract validation
entities.definition: Selected technical vertical slices and tests passed without establishing a universal execution abstraction or model equivalence.
entities.scope: Technical validation only.

entities.name: Production-learning integration evidence incomplete
entities.definition: Twenty-nine tracked records were available; a reported 1,016-run local artifact was unpublished and a later campaign was interrupted.
entities.scope: No completed independently verifiable campaign.

entities.name: Empirical vehicle feasibility screen only
entities.definition: The screening stopped at feasibility gates and produced no empirical outcome validation.
entities.scope: Candidate data feasibility only.

entities.name: State and trajectory support diagnostics
entities.definition: Finite gate diagnostics recorded support/discrimination limits; no confirmatory policy-value estimate was produced.
entities.scope: Technical gate only.

entities.name: Counterfactual engine equivalence gate failed
entities.definition: Control labels were not equivalent, so the proposed larger run received NO-GO and did not execute.
entities.scope: Technical negative; no policy-effect estimate.

entities.name: Contextual selection under changing rewards and selective feedback
entities.definition: Studies contextual action selection under nonstationary outcomes, selective observations, memory and assignment.
entities.scope: Distinct simulation factors and estimands; source campaign records are not combined into one effect.
assumptions: Reported algorithm variants are not all faithful implementations of named standard procedures.
Observation can be endogenous to assignment.

entities.name: Selective-feedback contextual selection effects are cell-specific
entities.definition: In one shared-feedback infrequent-change cell, a windowed method had regret 184.88 versus 259.47 (difference −74.59, interval [−89.60,−59.58]); closed-loop intervals included zero.
entities.scope: Exploratory cell-specific comparisons; not pooled across distinct estimands.
assumptions: The source record reports candidate algorithms that differ in more than memory.

entities.name: Static constrained assignment comparison
entities.definition: Exact finite comparison of task assignment choices under a static effectiveness objective.
entities.scope: Constructed finite allocation case; no temporal state transition.
assumptions: Constructed finite objective, action set and resource semantics as stated by the historical source.

entities.name: Static constrained assignment comparison reported exact values
entities.definition: Reported S1 value comparison: 2.6 versus 1.8.
entities.scope: Historical finite constructions; detailed execution artifacts are not retained on this branch.
assumptions: Values are scoped to their individual constructed cases.

entities.name: Shared-budget temporal optimization
entities.definition: Finite dynamic decisions with shared resource budgets and continuation value.
entities.scope: S2 cases are distinct constructions; Bellman and myopic values are not pooled into one estimator.
assumptions: Constructed finite objective, action set and resource semantics as stated by the historical source.

entities.name: Shared-budget temporal optimization reported exact values
entities.definition: Reported S2a exact 8 versus greedy 7.2; S2b Bellman 1 versus myopic .9 with sufficient budget 1.9.
entities.scope: Historical finite constructions; detailed execution artifacts are not retained on this branch.
assumptions: Values are scoped to their individual constructed cases.

entities.name: Load-only feasible queue dispatch
entities.definition: Selects an admissible agent using expected pending workload; ignores competence.
entities.scope: Historical model-specific policy; no claim of general optimality.
assumptions: No competence information is used.
entities.inputs: Queue state, eligibility and estimated workload

entities.name: Known-competence deadline dispatch
entities.definition: Ranks admissible agents by true task competence multiplied by estimated probability of on-time completion.
entities.scope: Historical model-specific policy; no claim of general optimality.
assumptions: True competence is available only to the information-complete reference.
entities.inputs: Task type, true competence and observable workload/service/deadline state

entities.name: Estimated-competence deadline dispatch
entities.definition: Uses the same competence-times-deadline score as the information-complete rule, substituting Beta-Bernoulli estimates updated on observed outcomes.
entities.scope: Historical model-specific policy; no claim of general optimality.
assumptions: No hidden competence or future outcome is observed.
entities.inputs: Task type, prior observed task outcomes, and observable operational state

entities.name: Contextual deadline dispatch
entities.definition: Adapts dispatch choices using a disjoint linear upper-confidence policy with context equal to deadline feasibility times task-family indicator.
entities.scope: Historical model-specific policy; no claim of general optimality.
assumptions: Feedback is updated only when its specified reward becomes observable.
entities.inputs: Observable context, delayed binary on-time-correct reward and feasibility state

entities.name: Same-agent multi-task assignment
entities.definition: Requires one agent identity to handle all task types in the static comparison.
entities.scope: Historical model-specific policy; no claim of general optimality.
assumptions: No learning or time evolution.
entities.inputs: Fixed effectiveness matrix and task demand
entities.outputs: Selected common agent and expected effectiveness

entities.name: Taskwise competence assignment
entities.definition: Allows the selected agent to vary by task type under the declared feasible access class.
entities.scope: Historical model-specific policy; no claim of general optimality.
assumptions: Feasible assignment/access class is declared; any convexification is separate.
entities.inputs: Fixed effectiveness matrix and task demand
entities.outputs: Task-specific agent choices and expected effectiveness

entities.name: Prospective computation selector
entities.definition: Selects additional computation from available prospective signals in a finite sequential problem-belief setting.
entities.scope: Historical model-specific policy; no claim of general optimality.
assumptions: Observed call rates differ from nominal target in the confirmatory comparison.
entities.outputs: Continue/stop or computation choice and terminal decision

entities.name: Synthetic joint classifier error laws
entities.definition: Finite joint Bernoulli error distributions with specified marginals and dependence.
entities.scope: Three classifier variables; exact probability law; majority decision.
assumptions: Constructed laws; no inference on real models.

scenario_contract.tasks: One common classification instance abstracted to correctness/error
scenario_contract.capabilities: Marginal error probability .20 for each classifier in the specified laws

entities.name: Synthetic transfer and classification tasks
entities.definition: Three generated binary classification tasks with separate train/validation/test examples and one donor-to-recipient distillation comparison.
entities.scope: Task distributions and the train/test overlap defect in the first iteration are methodologically relevant.
assumptions: V2 contrasts remain inconclusive; raw predictions are not retained.

scenario_contract.agents: Donor classifier A3 and recipient classifier A1, with other baseline models
scenario_contract.capabilities: Task-specific classifier performance and donor output probabilities

entities.name: Joint error and majority-risk model

entities.name: Finite service and assignment solver checks

assumptions: No common cross-case estimand is asserted.
